flashcards.front: What is the difference between an Expert System and a Machine Learning system?
flashcards.back: An Expert System uses hand-coded IF-THEN rules in a Knowledge Base executed by an Inference Engine. Machine Learning automatically learns decision boundaries by fitting parameters to empirical training data.

flashcards.front: What is Data Leakage in machine learning, and how does it happen in cybersecurity?
flashcards.back: Data leakage occurs when future information or ground-truth investigation artifacts contaminate training features. In cybersecurity, randomly shuffling time-series logs leaks future attack data into past predictions.

flashcards.front: How do K-Means and DBSCAN differ in handling outliers?
flashcards.back: K-Means forces all outliers into the nearest centroid cluster; DBSCAN identifies sparse points and explicitly flags them as Noise (-1), making DBSCAN superior for anomaly detection.

flashcards.front: What is the mathematical formulation of the Sigmoid function in Logistic Regression?
flashcards.back: P(y=1|x) = 1 / (1 + e^-z), where z = w^T x + b. It maps any real-valued number into a calibrated probability strictly bounded between 0 and 1.

flashcards.front: What are Support Vectors in an SVM?
flashcards.back: Support vectors are the critical training data points closest to the decision hyperplane that directly determine its position and maximize the margin width (2 / ||w||).

flashcards.front: Define Dwell Time and Flight Time in Keystroke Dynamics.
flashcards.back: Dwell Time = Key Release Time - Key Press Time (duration key held). Flight Time = Next Key Press Time - Previous Key Release Time (inter-key transition latency).

flashcards.front: What do FAR, FRR, and EER represent in biometric verification?
flashcards.back: FAR (False Acceptance Rate) = impostor accepted. FRR (False Rejection Rate) = genuine user rejected. EER (Equal Error Rate) = the operating threshold where FAR equals FRR.

flashcards.front: Why is Accuracy an invalid metric for evaluating fraud detection models?
flashcards.back: Because fraud is rare (<0.1%). A trivial dummy model predicting 'no fraud' achieves 99.9% accuracy while catching zero attacks (0% recall). Use Precision, Recall, and PR-AUC instead.

flashcards.front: What is the core difference between Bagging and Boosting?
flashcards.back: Bagging trains independent models in parallel on bootstrap samples to reduce variance (Random Forest); Boosting trains models sequentially, fitting residual errors to reduce bias (Gradient Boosting).

formulaSheet.name: Perceptron Weighted Sum & Activation
formulaSheet.formula: z = \sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i + b, \quad y = 1 \text{ if } z \ge 0 \text{ else } 0
formulaSheet.description: Linear decision threshold for binary classification in Unit 3.

formulaSheet.name: Perceptron Weight Update Rule
formulaSheet.description: Adjusts feature weight proportionally to prediction error and learning rate eta.

formulaSheet.name: SVM Maximum Margin Width
formulaSheet.description: The geometric separation between support vectors that SVM maximizes.

formulaSheet.name: Logistic Regression Sigmoid Probability
formulaSheet.description: Converts linear score into calibrated probability between 0 and 1 for phishing detection.

formulaSheet.name: Bayes' Theorem for Spam Detection
formulaSheet.formula: P(\text{Spam} | W) = \frac{P(W | \text{Spam}) \cdot P(\text{Spam})}{P(W | \text{Spam}) P(\text{Spam}) + P(W | \text{Legit}) P(\text{Legit})}
formulaSheet.description: Calculates posterior probability of spam given observed word frequencies.

formulaSheet.name: Entropy & Information Gain
formulaSheet.formula: H(S) = -\sum p_i \log_2 p_i, \quad IG(S, A) = H(S) - \sum \frac{|S_v|}{|S|} H(S_v)
formulaSheet.description: Measures impurity reduction for feature splitting in Decision Trees.

formulaSheet.name: Keystroke Timing Features
formulaSheet.description: Core temporal kinematic metrics in behavioral biometrics.

formulaSheet.name: Face Embedding Cosine Similarity
formulaSheet.description: Measures angular orientation between deep facial representation vectors.

formulaSheet.name: Biometric Error Rates (FAR & FRR)
formulaSheet.formula: \text{FAR} = \frac{\text{False Acceptances}}{\text{Total Impostor Attempts}}, \quad \text{FRR} = \frac{\text{False Rejections}}{\text{Total Genuine Attempts}}
formulaSheet.description: Standard performance measures for 1:1 biometric verification systems.

formulaSheet.name: Confusion Matrix Metrics (Precision, Recall, F1)
formulaSheet.description: Critical evaluation metrics under extreme class imbalance in fraud detection.

formulaSheet.name: Regression Error Metrics (MAE & RMSE)
formulaSheet.description: Measures error magnitude for incident volume and financial loss forecasting.
